Oct 9, 2026

Hosting selection and system simplification decided via strategic architecture review.

## **Hosting environment and infrastructure**

* Oyebode Oluwasanmi approved the Database M hosting plan due to cost efficiency compared to Azure.  
* Selected the 2-year professional Linux VPS plan costing \$259 with an ongoing discount.  
* Server specifications include 8 CPU cores, 18 GB RAM, 240 GB SSD, and bi-weekly USA backups.  
* Staging environment replicates full live capabilities including email functionality and pre-seeded data before production deployment.  
* Configured subdomains using hub for production and staging for the testing environment.

## **HR and administrative rules**

* Late arrival rules trigger automated queries when accumulated hours or days reach configured thresholds.  
* Payroll features maintain a simple structure with advanced tax and pension calculations under an advanced option.  
* Budget controls and budget-versus-actual tracking are omitted from expense modules to ensure operational simplicity.

## **Communication and mailboxes**

* Mailbox module belongs to milestone 1 under the community category supporting internal and external communications.  
* Mailbox connections utilize IMAP for inbound and SMTP for outbound traffic with preconfigured port settings.  
* Configuration panels allow users to connect mailboxes using email addresses, display names, and passwords.

## **AI integration and backend structure**

* Gemini powers AI functionalities through paid services rather than open-source alternatives.  
* Backend modules incorporate dedicated AI integration files across applicable system components.

* **Temporary Gmail Account Usage** The participants agreed to use a temporary Gmail account for the build period to streamline authentication and OTP verification.

* **Staging Environment Functional Scope** The team agreed that the staging environment will operate as a fully functional live site capable of sending emails prior to production deployment.

### **Details**

* **Environment and Hosting Setup**: JBS Praxis raised the need to discuss the hosting environment since project deadlines started counting following payment processing. JBS Praxis suggested setting up two subdomains from mycityapp.io—one for staging and one for production—using hub.mycityapp.io for production and a temporary staging subdomain that will be deleted post-launch. For physical hosting, JBS Praxis presented Database M, located in the United States, noting that local hosting companies like True Host are significantly more costly at roughly double the price ([00:00:13](#00:00:13)) ([00:03:44](#00:03:44)). Oyebode Oluwasanmi agreed to proceed with the Database M professional VPS plan priced at \$259 for a two-year term (featuring an ongoing 54% discount, 8 CPU cores, 18 gigabytes of RAM, 240 gigabytes of SSD, and 300 Mbps bandwidth) without shopping around further. Additionally, JBS Praxis and Oyebode Oluwasanmi agreed to create a temporary Gmail account for project signup to avoid constant verification and OTP hurdles, after which JBS Praxis will hand the account over ([00:06:12](#00:06:12)) ([00:08:47](#00:08:47)).

  ![][image1]

* **Domain Providers and Stakeholders Coordination**: Oyebode Oluwasanmi noted that they recently joined the organization and were unsure who the domain providers were or how subdomains are configured on mycityapp.io, committing to check with colleagues ([00:02:48](#00:02:48)) ([00:09:42](#00:09:42)). When JBS Praxis inquired if MTN Nigeria is connected to the project, Oyebode Oluwasanmi clarified that MTN is only developing the mobile app and is unconnected to the enterprise application software. Oyebode Oluwasanmi committed to emailing Cynthia (the operations and people lead) to ascertain domain hosting providers and request Excel trackers used prior to system building ([00:10:47](#00:10:47)). Furthermore, Oyebode Oluwasanmi added JBS Praxis to a WhatsApp group to facilitate urgent project communication ([00:11:42](#00:11:42)).

* **Hosting Pricing Comparison**: When Godwin-Okoh Elisha joined the meeting, they questioned whether the team was acquiring an Azure server. JBS Praxis clarified they selected Database M instead of Azure, explaining that Azure operates on a pay-as-you-go model and would cost nearly double or triple the price of Database M on an annual basis. Godwin-Okoh Elisha agreed that Database M is the better and less expensive choice ([00:15:20](#00:15:20)).

* **Late Arrivals and Rule Configuration**: JBS Praxis and Godwin-Okoh Elisha discussed how late arrivals generate queries ([00:15:20](#00:15:20)). JBS Praxis clarified that late arrivals do trigger system queries, but only when specific configured rules are met—such as accumulating a defined number of hours, days, or occurrences in a week. Godwin-Okoh Elisha and JBS Praxis confirmed that administrators can set up and configure these rules themselves ([00:17:21](#00:17:21)).

* **Staging Environment and Data Seeding**: JBS Praxis explained that the staging environment will function as a fully live site capable of sending emails and performing all real functions rather than a restricted environment, ensuring users experience the full platform before production deployment ([00:18:06](#00:18:06)). To prevent corrupting live data, JBS Praxis stated that staging will run migrations and pre-seeded data, which must be reviewed and approved by stakeholders before pushing to production ([00:18:54](#00:18:54)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha noted that production deployment will occur step-by-step rather than in a single run ([00:19:42](#00:19:42)).

* **Budget Controls and Expense Module Simplicity**: JBS Praxis discussed budget controls, arguing that adding budget versus actual variance tracking would overcomplicate the system given that the client aims for simplicity over rigid organizational structures ([00:19:42](#00:19:42)). JBS Praxis proposed omitting a separate cash request module and building only a simple expense module where approved expenses reflect actual operational needs without requiring prior monthly budgeting. Godwin-Okoh Elisha agreed with this simplified approach to avoid unnecessary complications ([00:20:36](#00:20:36)).

* **Mailbox Integration and Setup**: JBS Praxis stated that the mailbox feature must be included in milestone one under the community module, which handles both internal and external communications. JBS Praxis demonstrated how users will log in using their mycityapp.io email addresses and passwords ([00:21:27](#00:21:27)). To streamline user onboarding, JBS Praxis proposed creating a centralized setup configuration where SMTP and IMAP DNS records, ports (such as 993 and 465), and server hosts are pre-configured by administrators, preventing individual users from having to manually input connection ports. Godwin-Okoh Elisha and JBS Praxis agreed on implementing this setup console configuration ([00:22:20](#00:22:20)) ([00:24:35](#00:24:35)).

Godwin-Okoh Elisha confirmed that they are implementing an AI.js file for each backend module except those that do not require it ([00:27:05](#00:27:05)).

* **Payroll and Tax Rules**: JBS Praxis addressed tax rules, explaining that taxes and pensions will not be included in the basic setup but will instead be positioned behind an advanced payroll option. JBS Praxis noted that users can start with a simple payroll and switch to the advanced option if they require pension and tax calculations ([00:27:05](#00:27:05)).
